title: SoftHateBench: Evaluating Moderation Models Against Reasoning-Driven, Policy-Compliant Hostility
findings: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models performed relatively well at detecting explicit 'hard' hate speech targeting religious groups (specifically Religion/Belief and Race/Ethnicity domains). However, their performance degraded substantially when faced with 'soft' variants of hate speech, indicating a vulnerability to subtle, reasoning-driven hostility even in domains where they initially show strength.
